sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN lake.trips t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID AND t.payment_type = 2
GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone
ORDER BY z.LocationID

attempts.sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COALESCE(t.cnt, 0) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT PULocationID, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM lake.trips
    WHERE payment_type = 2
    GROUP BY PULocationID
) t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID
ORDER BY z.LocationID

attempts.sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN lake.trips t
  ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID::INTEGER
 AND t.payment_type = 2
GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone
ORDER BY z.LocationID
attempts.change_summary: Eliminated the runtime CAST by casting the zones.LocationID to INTEGER to match trips.PULocationID type, allowing a direct integer equality join.
attempts.detail: median 0.98×, saving -0.1 ms, 1/3 pairs faster — missed: ratio, floor, majority

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query scans the entire 495K-row trips table to apply the payment_type=2 filter (yielding ~99K rows), then performs a hash join with a CAST on the join key against the tiny 265-row zones table, followed by a hash aggregation of the 99K joined rows.

plan_nodes.note: Join Type: RIGHT | Conditions: CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID | Estimated Cardinality: 99167

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join lake.trips t on … and t.payment_type = 2)

The HASH_JOIN (node 8) incurs CPU overhead from the CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) in the join condition; if PULocationID and LocationID shared the same integral type the cast could be eliminated and the join could use a more efficient equality operator.

The left input SEQ_SCAN on trips reads all 495K rows because there is no index or zone-map on payment_type; a partial index on (payment_type, PULocationID) or partitioning by payment_type would allow skipping the 80% of rows that do not match payment_type=2.

The HASH_GROUP_BY following the join processes 99K rows only to reduce to 265 groups; pushing the aggregation into the trips scan (pre-aggregating cash trips per PULocationID) before the join would shrink the build side and avoid hashing 99K rows.
